title: sse: fix chunking/framing for partial JSON streams and token/event ordering
author: Ava Patel
release_notes: Fixes SSE streaming framing issues that could produce invalid partial JSON for structured output / function-calling. Improves delimiter ordering and token/event emission to avoid client-side parse errors. No API changes.
description: Context: customers and internal e2e tests have shown intermittent invalid partial-JSON events when using SSE streaming for structured output (function/tool calling, OpenAI-compat streaming). Root cause: the stream encoder could emit token events and chunk delimiters out-of-order under certain batching/flush timings, and delimiter insertion logic did not account for partial JSON tokens that cross buffer boundaries. This led to clients receiving partial JSON fragments or a delimiter line before the final token fragment, causing parse failures or mis-ordered function-call events. Summary of changes: 1) Rework stream framing state machine to separate token-buffer boundaries from delimiter emission; delimiters are now emitted only after the token buffer is fully flushed and an explicit chunk boundary is reached. 2) Ensure token-event ordering by assigning monotonically increasing event sequence IDs at the encoder boundary to preserve ordering when requests are batched across worker threads. 3) Add a small lookback buffer to detect JSON structural boundaries (braces, quotes, escapes) so we do not split inside multibyte/string tokens that would produce invalid partial JSON documents. 4) Update OpenAI-compat layer mapping to guarantee that delta events ("delta", "tool_call", "function_call") are emitted in canonical order and that the final "done" event contains the correct closing delimiter. 5) Add deterministic unit + integration tests for streaming partial JSON, new flaky-e2e that reproduces previous failure, and a stress test for token/event ordering. Checklist: - [x] Reproduce failure locally with new e2e harness - [x] Unit tests covering framing edge cases - [x] Integration tests for OpenAI-compat streaming - [x] CI green (required rerun for flaky test) - [x] Reviewed and approved by runtime owners How we validated: ran stress-e2e (1000 short streams, mixed structured outputs) against dedicated local runtime and observed zero parse failures; ran openapi-compat tests used by internal customers; added golden-stream snapshots to catch regressions. Backwards compatibility: no changes to REST API or wire protocol expected for well-behaved clients. This fixes edge-case behavior that previously produced invalid partial JSON. Migration: none. Notes: the new lookback buffer has a small CPU cost in high-throughput scenarios; we mitigated by making it lightweight and only enabled when structured-output or partial-json mode is active. If teams see measurable perf regressions on extremely high QPS non-structured workloads, we can gate it behind a config flag. Related: ENG-1245 (streaming stability), ENG-1308 (openai-compat streaming fixes), SUP-4421 (customer report).

review_comments: Liam Chen: Can you explain why sequence IDs are necessary? Would an atomic increment per worker be enough?

Ava Patel: We need a sequence at the encoder boundary because worker batching can reorder token writes during a flush; atomic increment at encoder ensures global ordering per response. Added tests that break when sequence ids removed.
Miguel Ortega: lgtm aside from one nit on the lookback buffer size. Consider making it configurable with a sane default.
Ava Patel: Added config option STREAM_LOOKBACK_MAX_BYTES=64 and kept default at 32. Updated docs and tests.
Sofia Martinez: Verified against customer repro and confirmed parse errors are gone. Approved.
